scope: The delivered and verified Secure Auth Handoff P1 deterministic security core, exactly as merged at that commit and tree: sinbad-ai-core/auth-handoff/handoff-v0.js, sinbad-ai-core/auth-handoff/index.js, tests/sinbad-auth-handoff-v0.test.js, docs/auth-handoff/AUTH_HANDOFF_P1.md. Pure logic: a grant bound to task, purpose, workspace, capability, call ceiling and time; a state machine; single-use and replay protection; expiry, stop and cleanup semantics; secret scanning, redaction and leak detection; a closed participation-safe event schema. Built as SINBAD TASK-12 through the accepted Participation Gate. Also accepted: the lifecycle evidence recorded for TASK-12 (PR linked, merge verified, post-merge CI verified, COMPLETED), recorded forward, not retroactively. Accepted on the reported test and CI evidence listed below.

evidence.tests: tests/sinbad-auth-handoff-v0.test.js: 25 of 25 passed on the PR branch; related suites (auth handoff, participation, lifecycle, evaluator, capture client, project2) 160 of 160; full local npm test 2531 tests = 2528 pass + 2 fail + 1 skipped, the 2 failures and the skip matching the earlier local-only pattern (CRLF hash tests, Docker unavailable), CI being the authority
evidence.mutationEvidence: 38 deliberate mutants, each breaking one security rule, were all caught by a failing test and none survived; the mutation script was a temporary scratchpad script and is NOT in the repository, so this result is reported, not reproducible from the repository

limitationsRemain: P1 proves the rules, not the transport: no loopback broker, no browser side
the aal2 step-up is a caller-supplied flag that the pure logic cannot verify
the call ceiling is enforced on the client side only; sinbad-answer has no per-caller call budget
memory wiping is a cleanup directive, not a guarantee
nonces are not generated here; a later phase must generate them with a cryptographically secure source
replay protection across process restarts needs a later phase to persist used authorization ids
the credential fingerprint is a value derived from a token; it stays internal and is never recorded
constant-time comparison is used but cannot be proven by a behavioural test
